 P.S.TO JUDGE mbr/
 A.V. RAMAKRISHNA PILLAI, J.
Aggrieved by the inaction on the part of the respondent panchayath in taking a decision on the application submitted by the petitioner, the petitioner has come up before this Court.
2. The petitioner is the working partner of Spice 7 Restaurant within the local limits of the 2nd respondent panchayath.
The petitioner's firm has been conducting the said restaurant with all the required licence since 2011 onwards and Ext.P4 trade licence was issued by the respondent panchayath for 2014-15.

The petitioner applied for trade licence for the year, 2015-16, as evidenced by Ext.P5 receipt; and the respondent panchayath issued Ext.P7 notice intimating that a complaint is received from the the local people alleging that the waste water from the petitioner's restaurant is ..2..
contaminating the water of their well.
According to the petitioner, he has erected waste water treatment plant in the premises, which conforms to the standard prescribed by the Pollution Control Board.

According to him, no waste water is discharged from the restaurant to the adjacent lands and the treated waste water is used for the purpose of watering plants in the petitioner's compound and there is no question of contamination of any drinking water in the well
arises.
The petitioner's grievance is that so far, no action whatsoever is taken on the trade licence application of the petitioner.
He further alleges that since the restaurant is functioning without trade licence, certain local people, having vested interest, are attempting to close down the restaurant.
According to the petitioner, the non consideration of trade licence application is dereliction of statutory duty caste on the respondent as per the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act.
Hence, this writ petition.

sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner ..3..
and the learned Government Pleader.
4.

As the limited prayer in this writ petition is for a consideration of the application for trade licence submitted by the petitioner, this Court is of the view that the writ petition can be disposed of even without issuing notice to respondents 2 and 3.

Therefore, the writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent panchayath to consider and pass appropriate orders on the application for renewal of trade licence, as evidenced by Ext.P5 receipt,
submitted by the petitioner within a period of one month.
Till the entire exercise is completed, the functioning of the petitioner's restaurant shall not be disturbed by the respondents.

Sd/-
A.V. RAMAKRISHNA PILLAI JUDGE bka/-
